entities.summary:
Margaret of Città di Castello, TOSD, was an Italian Catholic educator and a Dominican tertiary who became known for her deep faith and holiness despite being blind and having other physical disabilities. Born in the late 13th century, her life is a testament to the resilience of the human spirit. She was educated in the Dominican order and taught at the convent of her order, where she also served as a spiritual advisor to the local community.

Margaret's significance lies in her role as a symbol of hope and inspiration to the marginalized and oppressed. Her story has been passed down through the centuries, serving as a reminder of the power of faith and determination in the face of adversity.

Her legacy extends beyond her own lifetime, influencing the development of education and spirituality in Italy during the Middle Ages.

A striking testament to her enduring impact is the establishment of the Order of Preachers' schools in the region, which continue to provide education and spiritual guidance to this day.
